tactics.name: Resource Development
tactics.summary: How groups obtain drones, components and the money or partners behind them.

techniques.name: Acquire commercial off-the-shelf drones
Procure components through commercial supply chains
Receive drones, components or know-how from a state sponsor
Run in-house assembly or production

concern: Requests to identify suppliers, brokers or shipping routes for drones or components while avoiding export controls or sanctions screening.
Requests to plan covert procurement for an armed group, or to structure purchases so they are not traced.
legitimate: History and analysis of how armed groups have sourced drones, as documented in UN, CAR or academic reporting.
Export-control, sanctions and supply-chain policy research.

tactics.name: Modification
tactics.summary: Turning consumer aircraft into weapons or extending what they can carry.

techniques.name: Adapt commercial drones to carry and release payloads
Configure drones for one-way attack
Modify for extended range, endurance or payload

concern: Any request for build steps, designs, parts lists, files or measurements to make a drone carry, release or detonate a payload.
Requests to troubleshoot or optimise a weaponised drone, including framing as fiction, a game or 'for research'.
legitimate: Descriptions at the level found in news or policy reporting ("groups adapted hobby drones to drop small munitions").
Agricultural, delivery or search-and-rescue payload systems with no weapon context.

tactics.name: Reconnaissance
tactics.summary: Surveillance of forces, targets, police or rivals.

techniques.name: Battlefield surveillance of opposing forces
Pre-attack surveillance or target selection
Monitoring of law enforcement, rivals or territory

concern: Requests to plan drone surveillance of a specific person, facility, prison or security post, or to identify blind spots in its defences.
Requests to evade detection while surveilling a named site.
legitimate: Hobby photography, mapping and inspection questions under ordinary airspace rules.
Research on how surveillance drones changed small-unit warfare.

tactics.name: Delivery and Employment
tactics.summary: Using drones to attack, smuggle or disrupt.

techniques.name: Dropped-munition attacks on security forces
One-way drone attacks on infrastructure or bases
Attacks or plots against political leaders or VIPs
Contraband delivery into prisons
Cross-border smuggling of drugs or goods
Drones integrated with a ground assault
Disruption of airports or restricted airspace
Attacks causing civilian harm

concern: Requests for targeting help, attack planning, timing or flight planning against people, crowds, prisons, airports or infrastructure.
Requests to deliver items into a prison or across a border by drone without detection.
legitimate: Casualty, incident and trend analysis; journalism and court-record summaries.
Counter-drone, airport-safety and prison-security policy research at a defensive, non-operational level.

tactics.name: Propaganda and Influence
tactics.summary: Filming attacks and using aerial footage for messaging and recruitment.

techniques.name: Filming attacks for propaganda releases
Aerial footage for recruitment, branding or messaging
Symbolic or protest flights over sensitive sites

concern: Requests to script, edit or optimise attack footage for an armed group's channels, or to glorify a specific attack.
Requests to write recruitment content around drone operations for a designated group.
legitimate: Analysis of extremist media strategy, content-moderation research and media literacy work.
Lawful aerial filmmaking and protest-law questions.

tactics.name: Evasion
tactics.summary: Adapting to counter-drone defences and hiding operators.

techniques.name: Adapting operations in response to counter-drone measures
Concealing operators or launch sites, avoiding attribution

concern: Requests to defeat or bypass jamming, geofencing, Remote ID, detection systems or prison and airport counter-drone systems.
Requests to avoid identification after flying in restricted airspace.
legitimate: Policy discussion of the counter-drone arms race and its limits, as covered in public reporting.
Compliance questions about Remote ID, registration and no-fly zones.

tactics.name: Diffusion
tactics.summary: How methods spread between groups, sponsors and regions.

techniques.name: Sharing drone guidance through online channels or publications
Training provided by a state sponsor or partner group
Emulation of techniques across groups or regions

concern: Requests to write, translate, summarise or reformat drone weapon manuals or instructional posts for distribution.
Requests to design a training curriculum for an armed group's drone unit.
legitimate: Research on terrorist innovation and diffusion, and platform trust-and-safety work on removing such content.
Translation or summary of published policy research that is itself non-operational.
